Each highlight now gets its own quote note for your comment, PDFs can use dark pages, and Reader gains search, password entry, and many reading fixes.

Highlights and book notes:

- Each highlight gets a quote note beside the book note. It holds the quote and your comment below it. Quote notes are found by the highlight ID in their properties, so you can rename or move them. Deleting a highlight moves its quote note to the trash; **Undo** brings the comment back.
- Quotes in the book note link to their quote notes. The **Link quotes** setting is gone, since quotes now always link.
- The sidebar shows the passages as a flat list. Each passage shows its quote and comment, and you can edit the comment in place. Enter saves the comment and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Click a quote, or press Enter on it, to show the highlight in the PDF.
- New sections no longer get a `^block` ID under the quote. IDs written by earlier versions are removed the next time a book note updates.
- Book notes open in their own tab group beside the PDF.

Reading PDFs:

- Dark pages: choose **Always original colors**, **Follow Obsidian's color scheme** (the default), or **Always dark pages** in settings. Override it for one PDF with the page colors button in the Reader header or the **Toggle dark pages for this PDF** command. Pages no longer flash white while they draw.
- Search the document, open password-protected PDFs, see comments embedded in the PDF, and use Back/Forward to return to earlier positions. Form fields are marked on the page; click one to fill in the form in Obsidian's PDF viewer.
- Links inside PDFs work again.
- Search marks line up with ligatures, and repeated or wrapped results scroll into view.
- A link such as `[[Book.pdf#page=2]]` to a PDF already open in another tab now goes to that page.

Requires Obsidian desktop 1.14.4 or newer. Runtime verification covers Linux.
